items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: listen I played Lady and Trane and Miles and Prez

ctx.x: Well it varies from artist to artist. With David, he was open to me suggesting songs and he also listened to the radio so he didn’t just listen to jazz. So he was open. And when I started saying I don’t want to work with like jazz rhythm sections, I want to work with R&B studio cats like Bernard Purdie and Richard Tee and Eric Gale and Chuck Rainey. I want to work with those guys. But they had a very high level of musicianship beyond just, you know, playing on commercial records. The guys could play. So when they…

that. And also jazz radio at that time, listen I played Lady and Trane and Miles and Prez and you know like Ellington and Mingus, all that stuff. But the thrust of my show was the popular jazz of the day: Horace and Cannon and Blakey and you know, whoever had like a jazz hit or whoever had albums that went beyond the three, four, five thousand selling jazz records.
Did you ever butt heads with Bernard Purdie?
